card.name: Words just before a risk-of-developing clause
card.fires_on: Words like "more", "patients", "will" or "The" in warning text, right before a clause about who develops or is at risk of an adverse event. It marks the point where a risk, syndrome or complication is about to be named.

modes.label: More likely to be associated
modes.description: The word "more" in a comparison about which drugs are linked to an adverse condition.
modes.example: The information available does not identify any particular opioids as being<< more>> likely to be associated with adrenal insuff

modes.label: Patients who develop an event
modes.description: The word "patients" before a relative clause about those who experience or develop a serious reaction.
modes.example: Over 90% of carbamazepine treated<< patients>> who will experience SJS/TEN have

modes.label: Who will develop
modes.description: A word before a predicted outcome, such as "will" or a sentence-opening "The" before a risk statement.
modes.example: The risk appears to be highest among the elderly, especially elderly women, but it is impossible to predict, which patients<< will>> develop the syndrome.

card.writes: It suppresses words like worsen, exacerbate and severity, so the next word is likely something other than a worsening term.
card.plain: It fires in warnings just before the text says who gets an adverse event or how likely it is.
